findings.finding_id: plugin/skills/faff/bin/lib/validate-adapters.js::per-line scan misses a fenced/continued commissaire --issue invocation
findings.title: per-line scan misses a fenced/continued commissaire --issue invocation
findings.disposition_rationale: Per-line scan is the spec's explicit chosen design (WHAT match-predicate + HOW), mirroring the FAFF-1198 removed-dispatch-key lint; the helper comment documents the single-line assumption. Real commissaire invocations in faff prose are single-line backticked commands, so the guard covers the actual surface. Precision-over-recall: a missed wrapped form is a smaller harm than a false CI FAIL.

occurrences.title: per-line scan misses a fenced/continued commissaire --issue invocation

findings.title: lookbehind excludes ./faff path-prefixed binary spelling
findings.disposition_rationale: ./faff is outside the spec's enumerated binary forms (faff, "$faff", "$FAFF", $faff); faff prose uses "$faff"/faff for commissaire. The lookbehind dot avoids matching faff as a dotted-identifier suffix. Precision-over-recall.

findings.finding_id: test/validate-adapters-commissaire-unit-id.test.mjs::negative tests pass vacuously if the run crashes
findings.title: negative tests pass vacuously if the run crashes
findings.disposition_rationale: Added a ran(r) anchor (r.error==null && /RESULT:/.test(stdout)) to every negative, so a no-finding can only mean the lint ran to completion past the guard, not that it crashed before reaching it.
